title: Fab City Index Cell
description: One cell of the 4x5 pillar x scale matrix, saying what it would take to fill it. Entries say what a source carries; a cell says what the Index claims when that cell is populated, what the minimum is, and — the field that matters most — what it does NOT claim. Each cell lives at cells/{pillar}-{scale}.yaml, lowercase, matching its own `cell` key; scripts/validate.py checks that the filename and the key agree.

cell.description: The cell key in the node's own spelling: Pillar|Scale, capitalised, pipe-separated — the same strings an entry's `feeds_cells` uses, so the two join without a translation table.

indicator_categories.description: The families of indicator this cell is for, in words a person uses: 'air quality', 'material throughput', 'procurement openness'. Broad on purpose — an entry is filed against a named row, and this is the list of rows that exist here.

name.description: The indicator, named the way it would be read off a dashboard.

unit.description: The unit it is carried in, explicitly. 'ug/m3', 't/capita/yr', 'count', 'percent'. A number without a unit is not an indicator.

aggregation.description: How readings become the cell's number: mean, median, sum, max, p95, annual-total, latest. Says what the cell is doing to the data, which is the half of an index that is usually left implicit.

minimum_indicators.description: The floor. Below this list the cell is not filled, it is decorated — a single source with one reading is a demo, and this repo has been burned by cells that looked live on the strength of one row.

does_not_claim.description: What a filled version of this cell must not be read as saying. Required, and required to be specific: a city-scale air-quality cell full of reference-station data does not claim neighbourhood exposure; an economic cell built from registered businesses does not claim informal production. This is the field that keeps an index from being asked to answer questions it cannot.

notes.description: Anything else: which territories have a candidate source for this cell, where the aggregation is contested, what the known gap is.
